map.Review: Fractions & Decimals — part of T: Review: Fractions & Decimals — part of The Pattern Engine arc. ½-benchmark fractions · add/subtract decimals. Read from start to end. Each gate gives hints and a worked example. It never blocks the page.
map.Episode 1. Same crew, same city — one fo: Episode 1. Same crew, same city. One part of the case. Turn the page when you are ready.
map.That dome! The door's propped open — GO: That dome! The door is open. GO GO GO!
map.Vexhall Observatory? Sealed since foreve: Vexhall Observatory? Shut for ages. Five stars for spooky.
map.I'm Maya — that's Theo, Zara, and Dev. W: I'm Maya. That's Theo, Zara, and Dev. We come in peace. And puddles.
I know. Librarians know it all. I'm Ms. Ortiz. Welcome to Vexhall.
map.Vexhall Observatory — built by Ada Vex,: Vexhall Observatory was built by Ada Vex, a math builder. She made half of Axiom City. Then she went missing.
map.Inside: brass, dust, and ten thousand bo: Inside: brass, dust, and ten thousand books.
map.Ada Vex's last journal. Sealed sixty yea: Ada Vex's last journal. Shut for sixty years. The clasp opens only for the right fraction.
map.Three engravings — and one instruction:: Three engravings and one rule: "FEED ME THE ONE BELOW ONE-HALF."
map.Use a benchmark — test each fraction aga: Use a benchmark. Test each fraction against 1/2. Is the top number more or less than half the bottom?
map.Uh… did the lamps just blink three times: Uh… did the lamps just blink three times, then nine, then twenty-seven?
map.A benchmark is a friendly reference numb: A benchmark is a friendly number, like 1/2. You compare other numbers to it.
map.Reader — you're the fifth crew member no: Reader, you are the fifth crew member now. Feed the clasp the right fraction.
map.The clasp offers 3/8, 5/9, 7/12 and dema: The clasp shows 3/8, 5/9, 7/12. It wants the one below one-half. Then it checks your thinking. Tap one answer in each row.
map.CLASP A — WHICH FRACTION IS LESS THAN 1/: CLASP A — WHICH FRACTION IS LESS THAN 1/2?
map.CLASP B — IS 5/9 CLOSER TO 1/2 OR TO 1?: CLASP B — IS 5/9 CLOSER TO 1/2 OR TO 1?
map.Conceptual: compare each fraction to the: Conceptual: compare each fraction to the benchmark 1/2. A fraction is less than 1/2 when its numerator is less than HALF its denominator.
map.Procedural: half of 8 is 4. Half of 9 is: Procedural: half of 8 is 4. Half of 9 is 4.5. Half of 12 is 6. Compare each numerator to that half. For Clasp B, find how far 5/9 is from 1/2 and from 1.
map.Beneath the reading room. The journal's: Under the reading room. The journal's map points DOWN.
map.A door with a combination. Ada didn't tr: A door with a code. Ada did not trust keys, I guess.
map.Decimal dials. Easy to wreck if you don': Decimal dials. Easy to break if you ignore place value.
map.Write 3.6 as 3.60 — give it a hundredths: Write 3.6 as 3.60. Give it a hundredths digit. Add tenths to tenths, and hundredths to hundredths.
map.The door is humming. Doors should NOT hu: The door is humming. Doors should NOT hum.
map.A decimal names part of a whole by place: A decimal names part of a whole by place value. 3.6 means 3 ones and 6 tenths. It has the same value as 3.60.
map.Dial carefully, reader. This door has op: Dial with care, reader. This door has opinions.
map.Two decimal dials, one rule: \"Sum, then: Two decimal dials, one rule: "Sum, then difference." Find 3.6 + 2.85 and 12.5 − 4.75 to open the door.
map.Conceptual: decimals add and subtract li: Conceptual: decimals add and subtract like whole numbers IF every digit is in its place-value column. Give 3.6 a hundredths digit: 3.60.
map.Procedural: Dial 1: 3.60 + 2.85 — add hu: Procedural: Dial 1: 3.60 + 2.85. Add hundredths, then tenths, then ones. Dial 2: 12.50 − 4.75. You will need to regroup.
map.The full story — The Pattern Engine — is: The full story, The Pattern Engine, glows at the city gate. — A.V.
map.completed Unit 1 · Episode 1: Benchmark: completed Unit 1 · Episode 1: Benchmark & Brass in The Pattern Engine arc. They showed mastery of ½-benchmark fractions · add/subtract decimals.

map.A practice clasp offers 2/5 and 4/7, ask: A practice clasp shows 2/5 and 4/7. It wants the one below 1/2.
map.Half of 5 is 2.5 — and 2 < 2.5, so 2/5 s: Half of 5 is 2.5. And 2 < 2.5, so 2/5 is below the benchmark.
map.Half of 7 is 3.5 — and 4 > 3.5, so 4/7 s: Half of 7 is 3.5. And 4 > 3.5, so 4/7 is above. Feed it 2/5.
map.Your turn — same idea, different numbers: Your turn. Same idea, new numbers:
map.What numerator makes ?/8 land exactly ON: What numerator puts ?/8 exactly ON the 1/2 benchmark?
map.Write 2.4 as 2.40 so the hundredths line: Write 2.4 as 2.40 so the hundredths line up: 2.40 + 1.35.
map.Add by place: 0+5 hundredths, 4+3 tenths: Add by place: 0+5 hundredths, 4+3 tenths, 2+1 ones → 3.75. The dial turns.
map.Both clasps need a choice — tap one butt: Both clasps need an answer. Tap one button in each row.
map.Clasp A stays shut. Test your pick: is i: Clasp A stays shut. Check your pick. Is its numerator more or less than half its denominator?
map.Clasp B stays shut. 5/9 is only a sliver: Clasp B stays shut. 5/9 is just a little above 1/2. Measure both distances first.
map.3/8 < 1/2 (3 is less than 4), and 5/9 hu: 3/8 < 1/2 (3 is less than 4), and 5/9 is close to the 1/2 benchmark. The clasp springs open!
map.6.45 and 7.75 — the dials clack, the bra: 6.45 and 7.75. The dials click. The brass door rolls open!
map.A dial sticks. Line up the decimal point: A dial sticks. Line up the decimal points, tenths under tenths. Then work place by place.
Yes! Now go back and open that gate.
